lore: The coelacanth was known only from fossils and thought extinct for 66 million years, until a living specimen was hauled up off South Africa in 1938. A lobe-finned fish more closely related to lungfish and tetrapods than to most other fish, it moves its paired fleshy fins in a walking rhythm. By day it shelters in deep volcanic caves, drifting out at night to hunt along the slopes.
